title: Solar farm site selection with GIS and interconnection data
description: Screen buildable acres, compare points of interconnection, and verify solar export capacity. See what changed between two PJM study phases at one substation.
coverAlt: Chart of PJM allocated interconnection cost estimates at Nottingham 138 kV. The original request rose from $2.33 million to $4.16 million. Its 200 MW uprate rose from $2.68 million to $6.34 million.
coverCaption: PJM Transition Cycle 2 estimates at Nottingham 138 kV, Ohio. The chart compares allocations published in October 2025 and June 2026.
intro: Before you option land for a utility-scale solar farm, check whether the tract fits the proposed array and whether the grid can take the project’s output on your schedule. Use GIS to calculate contiguous buildable acreage and map routes to candidate connections. Then verify the exact point of interconnection, requested export in MW AC, upgrade costs, and schedule against the operator’s studies and project agreement.
takeaways: Keep the buildable polygons, the exclusions that produced them, and the largest contiguous area. The acreage on an assessor record cannot tell you what fits.
Use line and substation maps to find connection candidates. Verify the terminal or line tap, the route from the project, and the export case with the transmission provider.
Carry forward the latest study version and scope. At one Ohio substation, the estimate for a 200 MW solar uprate went from $2.68 million to $6.34 million between PJM study phases.

sections.heading: Calculate buildable acres inside the land you can control

blocks.text: Start with the surveyed or cadastral boundary and the parcels you can actually assemble. Mark gaps, easements, and access you would need across other land. Set a preliminary slope and grading tolerance with the layout engineer. Keep terrain, mapped wetlands, flood hazards, setbacks, and permit constraints as separate layers so the team can see and revise each assumption.

rows: Land and site control
County parcel GIS, assessor records, recorded plats and easements, and the current local siting rules.
Parcel IDs and boundaries, control dates, known easements, and the jurisdiction responsible for each approval.
Slope and grading
USGS 3DEP elevation. Choose the best available resolution for the site and check it against a survey before design.
Slope raster, elevation resolution and vintage, the assumed slope limits, and areas that need a grading check.
Water and hazards
U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service wetland mapping and FEMA’s National Flood Hazard Layer.
Mapped wetland and flood polygons, map dates, any screening buffers, and areas to verify in the field.
Solar resource and layout
National Solar Radiation Database weather and irradiance, a preliminary array layout, and site access plans.
Resource dataset and weather years, MW DC, inverter MW AC, usable blocks, and space for roads, drainage, and equipment.
Connection route
Transmission-owner maps and records, local parcel geometry, and the applicable generator interconnection queue.
Candidate connection, likely transmission owner, plausible lead-line route, and the parcels or rights of way the route crosses.

blocks.text: Intersect each exclusion with the tract, merge the overlapping exclusions, and subtract their combined area using a local projected coordinate system suited to measuring acreage. Say a 960-acre tract has 150 acres above your slope limit and 120 acres in a preliminary wetland exclusion, with 45 acres that satisfy both. The combined exclusion is 225 acres, leaving 735 acres for further screening. A layout with a largest contiguous block of 410 acres has a different design problem from a single 735-acre block. These numbers are illustrative. Keep each disconnected block, then test roads, drainage, equipment, and grading on the layout.

sections.heading: What establishes solar export capacity at a substation?

blocks.text: A transmission map can show that a line crosses the property. A queue can show who has applied and what the operator has published about those applications. To underwrite export, identify the exact connection and ask the operator which service, study assumptions, upgrades, and operating limits apply to your request. Ask for the date of the evidence and any conditions on construction and operation.

items: Record the proposed export at the connection in MW AC. Track panel nameplate in MW DC and inverter rating separately. For co-located batteries, also specify import, discharge, plant controls, and which resources can operate at the same time.
Name the substation bus or line tap, voltage, transmission owner, and proposed generator lead. Trace a viable route and identify crossings or easements that could delay it.

Check the operator’s queue and study versions by request ID. Capture earlier requests the study depends on, other affected transmission systems, required upgrades, cost allocation, and who is responsible for building what.

Get the latest applicable study, agreement, and upgrade schedule before treating an export assumption as committed. Confirm the applicable operating limits, milestones, and deliverability terms with the operator.

blocks.text: The public queue is useful when an option period is short. It can help focus questions and reveal competing or dependent requests. Each entry has a status and a reporting date. A withdrawn project’s requested MW cannot be treated as capacity available to your tract. For distribution-connected projects, start with the serving utility and its applicable process.

sections.heading: At Nottingham 138 kV, the same uprate got a higher estimate

blocks.text: PJM studied two linked requests from Energy Pastures Solar Project in Harrison County, Ohio. AG2-082 was the original 200 MW request. AH1-580 requested a 200 MW increase at the same point of interconnection. The 400 MW maximum facility output on the AH1-580 report includes the original 200 MW. Adding that 400 MW to the original 200 MW would count the original request twice.

rows: AG2-082 · original 200 MW
AH1-580 · 200 MW uprate

blocks.text: The uprate still requested 200 MW of energy service in Phase II. Its allocated physical network upgrade line increased from $2.326 million to $4.575 million, and the new estimate included $609,937 for transmission-owner interconnection facilities. Phase I had recorded zero on that facilities line and said that the physical facilities study would begin in Phase II. Carry the scope and stage beside the number. A zero from an earlier study may describe what has been priced so far.

We used the project allocation total as printed in each report. Those totals are estimates for those requests. The Phase II reports used a 2028 model base case. A separate agreement and project schedule would establish rights and milestones. The study figures cannot establish remaining capacity for a new applicant at Nottingham.

sections.heading: Which GIS tools and APIs fit a solar developer’s workflow?

blocks.text: Use public GIS layers when you need to run your own polygon calculations. PVcase Prospect documents a greenfield workflow for filtering by buildable acres and working with site constraints. Geoforge’s example report shows how a separate power screen can organize modeled headroom, queue records, and upgrades. Ask each provider which cases it covers and which results you can export with dates and sources.

Invariant Earth publishes fields for elevation, slope, wetland and flood indicators, and distance to transmission lines and substations. Use point fields to enrich a search, then use the tract and layout polygons to calculate buildable acreage. When evaluating an API, ask for the original source and geometry, the units, and the behavior when data is missing. Invariant publishes this guide. We checked the listed capabilities against public documentation.

A useful shortlist lets the next reviewer recreate the decision. Save the parcel and buildable geometry, the assumed project layout, and one record per candidate connection. Give each record a source, date, proposed MW, study stage, estimated upgrades, and open items. Before a land option goes hard, assign a person and due date to the evidence that could change your decision.

faqs.answer: Use the parcel boundary as the starting geometry. Subtract the union of exclusions and project setbacks, then keep both the total remaining area and the contiguous blocks. Check the preliminary result against site control, a layout, local requirements, and field surveys.

faqs.answer: A nearby power line gives you a candidate to investigate. Confirm the actual connection configuration, who owns the line, how the project can reach it, and whether the operator’s study supports the requested export under its modeled conditions.

faqs.question: Why are the PJM MW Energy and MW Capacity fields different?
faqs.answer: PJM reports the MW in the energy request separately from the MW it recognizes as Capacity in the study. AH1-580 lists a 200 MW energy request and a 134 MW Capacity increase. Its 400 MW maximum facility output refers to the combined facility after the proposed uprate.

title: Battery storage site selection for charging and discharge
description: Screen utility-scale battery sites for import and export MW, usable charging hours, queue dependencies, and grid upgrades. Compare three public studies.
coverAlt: Illustrative chart at a 50 MW import limit and 90% round-trip efficiency. Eight hours of charging supports 360 MWh of export and leaves a 40 MWh shortfall. Nine hours supports the 400 MWh target.
coverCaption: Illustrative recharge screen at the point of interconnection. A 50 MW import cap gives very different results when the battery can charge for eight hours or nine.
intro: A utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) needs a connection that can take power from the grid when the project plans to charge and deliver power back when it plans to discharge. Screen those two directions separately. Record the point of interconnection, the allowed hours and operating conditions for each direction, and the upgrades and dates that apply. Then check whether the permitted charging window can refill enough energy for the discharge you plan to sell.
takeaways: Ask the operator for maximum net import and export in MW at the same connection point, with dates, operating limits, and the documents behind both values.
A 100 MW battery that needs to deliver 400 MWh takes nearly nine hours to refill from empty at a 50 MW import cap and 90% meter-to-meter efficiency.

Keep MW, MWh, and service rights separate in the site record. The report for a 55 MW Virginia battery indicates grid charging in its project summary and leaves the numeric import limit unresolved at that level.

sections.heading: What should a utility-scale battery site screen include?

blocks.text: Start with the operating plan. State the planned discharge in MW, how many hours it must last, the energy available at the meter in MWh, and which hours the project needs to recharge. Identify the grid connection so both studies refer to the same physical point. If solar shares the connection, specify whether the battery can charge from the solar array, the grid, or both. Include the maximum simultaneous net export from the entire site.

rows: Charge from the grid
Net import MW, import hours by season, limits during peak load or outages, and any restrictions on grid charging.
Charging cases and operating assumptions, with the applicable service or agreement terms from the operator.
Discharge to the grid
Net export MW, usable MWh at the meter, export duration, applicable curtailment, and commercial service requested.
Export cases and agreement, including the limits at the proposed point of interconnection and any deliverability terms.
Check the queue and upgrades
Shared connection point, earlier requests the study depends on, upgrade owner, cost allocation, and the date each upgrade is needed.
The operator’s queue and dated study revisions, facilities scope, and schedule for construction and energization.
Check land and access
Controlled acreage, equipment and access layout, flood and drainage constraints, fire access and spacing, and the route of the lead line.
A layout tied to the actual parcels, local planning and fire requirements, and the easements needed for the route.

blocks.text: FERC’s Order No. 2023 directs U.S. transmission providers using the applicable procedures to study storage with assumptions that reflect proposed charging behavior, subject to reliability and good utility practice. Ask the provider which tariff and process apply to the particular connection and whether you need separate charging service. Capture the actual hours, limits, and conditions in the documents that will govern operation.

sections.heading: Three public studies show three kinds of charging evidence

rows: Tupelo Storage · Virginia · PJM 2026
55 MW maximum facility output and 220 MWh battery specification.
The project summary says grid charging is planned. The summary gives no numeric import MW.
Ask for the charging case and import terms. PJM’s Phase II cost summary allocates an estimated $7.64 million to this request.
Deka Road · Pennsylvania · PJM 2011
3 MW studied injection. PJM recognized zero MW as Capacity in the study and described the export as curtailable for reliability.
3.6 MW studied load at the same existing 69 kV connection.
The two directional values differ. Preserve the connection arrangement and the study’s stated treatment of export.
Oneida Energy Storage · Ontario · IESO 2022
250 MW injection evaluated in the study scope. The stated project rating was 250 MW and 1,000 MWh.
250 MW withdrawal evaluated in the same assessment.
Conditional approval carried connection requirements. Certain outage conditions limited the equipment’s ability to provide maximum active power alongside required reactive power.

blocks.text: At Oneida, the grid operator required reactive power capability equal to 33% of rated active power at the transformer terminals. It found 28.4% under the typical voltage condition it assessed at maximum injection. Reactive power helps control voltage and affects how much equipment capacity remains for active power. The assessment required the applicant to address that shortfall. Oneida later reported starting commercial operation in May 2025. The study figures above describe the proposed project and study conditions in 2022.

The practical test for a new site is to ask which limits already apply, which depend on planned equipment, and which conditions would reduce either direction. For queue records, save the project ID, resource type, stage, related requests, study date, and document URL. For an upgrade, keep the cost estimate vintages and responsibility for construction beside the expected service date.

sections.heading: Can a 50 MW import limit refill a 100 MW battery overnight?

blocks.text: Consider two illustrative battery sites that each need to export 100 MW for four hours and can import up to 50 MW when charging is permitted. Assume 400 MWh of usable export energy, an empty usable energy window at the start, and a constant 90% round-trip efficiency measured at the connection point. To calculate the export energy the charging window can support, multiply 50 MW by the allowed hours and 0.90, up to the battery’s 400 MWh usable limit.

blocks.text: The battery needs about 444 MWh of grid energy and 8 hours, 53 minutes, and 20 seconds at full import to refill from empty. Nine hours leaves little margin. Check the allowed hours against seasonal restrictions, the state of charge at the start of each dispatch cycle, and end-of-life usable capacity. A commercial model should also account for charge ramp, losses across operating conditions, and which hours have power available at an acceptable price.

sections.heading: How to compare candidate battery sites before signing an option

blocks.text: Use parcel boundaries, terrain, flood layers, and transmission maps to check the land and map viable connection routes. Use the operator’s queue and studies at each proposed point to identify other projects and upgrades. A substation distance field is useful for finding candidates. A dated charge and discharge case is what helps the team compare two sites with similar distances.

Send the same operating request for each candidate. State the MW and MWh at the meter, the charging schedule, the expected start date, and how operation changes under outages. Ask the operator to return the cases and documents behind each answer, the earliest date each direction can operate, and the cost and schedule of shared or assigned upgrades. Keep unknown values visible in the shortlist so a reviewer can tell where the investment case relies on unverified service.

faqs.question: Does a 100 MW battery always need 100 MW of charging capacity?
faqs.answer: Charge MW depends on how much energy the battery needs to restore and how long it can charge. A 400 MWh export target with 90% round-trip efficiency needs about 444 MWh of imported energy from empty. At 50 MW, that requires nearly nine hours at full import.

faqs.question: Can a generator interconnection queue tell me how much a battery can charge?
faqs.answer: A queue may list the battery’s size, resource type, and application status. Look for separate numeric import MW and operating conditions in the project’s study and applicable service documents. Some study summaries identify grid charging without stating the allowed import MW.

faqs.question: How do I compare a standalone battery with solar plus storage?
faqs.answer: Compare net import and simultaneous net export at the same point of interconnection. For a hybrid, specify whether the battery can charge from the grid and how the controls share the connection with solar. Document the operating limits the provider actually studied and the conditions attached to any agreement.

title: Retail site selection APIs for trade areas and foot traffic
description: Compare retail locations with travel-time areas, dated store openings, and comparable visit counts. A Harlem case shows how to use public transit data.
coverAlt: Aerial map of two 125th Street subway complexes and Trader Joe’s Harlem. From September 2023 to September 2024, estimated A, B, C and D station entries rose 17.6 percent, and 2 and 3 station entries rose 18.0 percent.
coverCaption: Transit context on 125th Street in Harlem. Station points and entry estimates from the MTA. Store location from NYC GeoSearch. Aerial imagery from NYS ITS Geospatial Services, 2024.
intro: Before signing a retail lease, find out who can reach the site, where customers at comparable stores actually come from, and what happened as nearby stores opened or closed. Those questions call for different data. Use routing for travel-time areas, a dated place directory for nearby stores, and comparable visit or pedestrian counts for activity. Keep the area, measure, and time window with every number so you can rerun the comparison.
takeaways: Draw candidate areas using the same travel mode and time. For existing stores, use visitor origins to learn where customers may actually come from.
Confirm openings and closures with dated retailer, landlord, or local records. A database creation date records when the entry appeared in that system.

At two 125th Street subway complexes in Harlem, entries grew about 18% between September 2023 and September 2024. Both are public measures of transit activity. They cannot tell you how many people visited the grocery store that opened nearby.

sections.heading: Which APIs answer each retail site question?

rows: Who can reach the site in ten minutes?
Esri routing service areas for walking or driving. Use Census ACS estimates to describe households within a defined area.
Use the actual customer entrance, travel mode, network vintage, and time-of-day assumptions. Ask how the provider assigns partially overlapping Census areas and shows uncertainty.
Where do people who visit a comparable store come from?
Placer’s Trade Area report for estimated visitor origins. Its glossary distinguishes visits, unique visitors, and the sampled device panel.
Request the store-level boundary and date range. Check how repeat trips are counted, what is suppressed, and which histories can be regenerated with a common model.
Which nearby stores opened or closed?
Foursquare Open Source Places for location identity and dated releases. Verify events with dated first-party or public records.
Match brand, address, unit, and coordinates. Keep the date the place entered the dataset and the verified operating date as separate fields.
How busy is the corridor at comparable times?
Municipal pedestrian counts or transit agency data. NYC DOT counts pedestrians at sampled locations and the MTA publishes station entry estimates.

Require a defined entrance, count line or property boundary. Preserve hours, days, and the instrument’s definition. For a specific storefront, ask for a comparable venue visit series or a direct count.

blocks.text: For a new site, estimate the reachable area from its entrance and compare it with existing stores of the same format. For an operating store, a share of visits can be traced to aggregate origin areas if the provider offers that report. The network polygon estimates access. The visitor-origin polygon describes where an observed or estimated customer base comes from. Keep both geometries if your team uses both.

sections.heading: What changed near two Harlem locations?

blocks.text: Trader Joe’s opened on West 125th Street in Harlem in July 2024. The National Urban League recorded the announcement that month, and the retailer lists the store at 123 West 125th Street. We used MTA station IDs to match two complexes along the corridor across years. The store address was geocoded through NYC GeoSearch. The comparison uses the station complexes as two observations and keeps the store as a separate record.

Each number represents estimated entries to a subway complex in that month. The MTA includes qualifying free transfers from outside the complex in the entry total, so adding the transfers field again would double count them. We use September in all four years to hold the month and its length constant. The weekday and weekend mix can still differ.

Both complexes grew at nearly the same percentage rate in the first comparison, even though one serves a different set of lines farther west. In the following year the A/B/C/D complex rose about 1.2%, while the 2/3 complex rose about 11.5%. The similarity in year one and divergence in year two show why it helps to look beyond a single station and a single period. An impact estimate for the store would require comparable venue visits or direct counts and a separate analysis of what else changed.

sections.heading: Build a store history you can compare across markets

blocks.text: Create a stable store identity for each location and link it to the lease unit and parcel. When a competitor moves, keep the old site record and the new site record with their respective dates. Save the source and observation time each time you see a change. For an opening, use the best documented public operating date and retain the actual precision, whether it’s a day, a month, or a range.

For visit trends, use the same source and venue boundary for each period. Match operating hours and the weekday and weekend mix where possible. Record holidays, construction, closures, and changes in sampling. For a store inside a mall, test whether the provider measures the store, the common corridor, or the entire property. Ask whether low sample counts are marked or withheld and whether the provider can reproduce an older estimate.

For household and demographic change, use comparable Census geographies and nonoverlapping ACS five-year periods, and keep the margins of error. Those estimates describe people and households in an area. To calculate sales conversion, use store visits and transactions measured for the same doors, dates, and hours.

sections.heading: What to ask for in a vendor trial

blocks.text: Give each provider three sites where you know something about what happened. Choose a standalone location, a store within a larger property, and a competitor that recently moved. Ask for an export with the store identity, the mapped boundary, the date and definition of each observation, and the results for the same two periods. Check the latest result against a dated store listing or your own counts. Test how the provider handles the old location after a move.

Invariant Earth publishes parcel, building, and road context fields for coordinate-based screening. You can use those fields to help resolve the property, then join a routing, visit, or place history product using its appropriate geometry. Invariant publishes this guide. The provider comparison uses public documentation. The Harlem calculation uses open MTA records and does not rely on a commercial visitor estimate.

description: Link an industrial parcel to EPA facility IDs and state permits. A Brooklyn case shows why address and boundary searches can miss regulatory records.

intro: To find environmental permits and enforcement history for an industrial site, start with the tax parcel and the operator’s names and addresses. Link those to the EPA Facility Registry Service ID and each program’s permit or handler ID. takeaways: Keep the tax lot, physical facility, regulated operator, and individual program identifiers as distinct records. A facility can use several addresses and share its site with other operators.
At Newtown Creek in Brooklyn, a boundary-only search would miss two of seven coordinate-bearing EPA records already linked to the facility.
Keep the observation date and document status with each result. A compliance status, a later notice, and a draft permit answer different questions.

sections.heading: Where to find industrial permit and enforcement records

rows: What property is in the transaction?
County or city cadastral GIS and assessor records. Use the survey, lease, and property documents for the actual area under review.
Parcel ID, boundary and version, site address aliases, operator names, and the relationship between the owned or leased area and the facility.
Which regulatory programs list the facility?
EPA Facility Registry Service and the program links in ECHO. Search the state’s permit inventory as well.
The EPA registry ID and separate air, water, and waste identifiers with their operator, site address, and reference-point description.
What does the permit allow or require?
The issuing agency’s final permit and modifications. In New York, start with the Department of Environmental Conservation’s permit and map indexes.
Permit type, the effective version and dates, authorized activities or units, applicability, and any conditions that matter to the planned use.
What enforcement or cleanup records exist?
EPA ECHO for program-specific notices, inspection summaries, and actions. Check the issuing agency for the original documents. Check state cleanup and federal Superfund records separately.
Program, event type, case ID and date, disposition where documented, and the geography or activity the record covers.

blocks.text: Use coordinates to find candidate matches. Verify a match with other fields such as program identifiers, address aliases, and the operator on the source document. Keep the original identifiers even when you display one facility. For a campus or a multi-tenant property, check which facility areas or units each document actually covers.

sections.heading: Newtown Creek shows what a boundary-only search misses

blocks.text: NYC GeoSearch returned borough-block-lot 3025250001 for 329 Greenpoint Avenue. MapPLUTO 26v2 lists that lot at 327 Greenpoint Avenue. A 2004 New York State DEC ruling lists the Newtown Creek plant at 329–69 Greenpoint Avenue and pairs DEC facility ID 2-6101-00025 with water permit NY0026204. Looking up that permit in EPA ECHO returns registry ID 110000561268, whose street address is 301 Greenpoint Avenue.

rows: NYC tax lot
MapPLUTO 26v2 provides the boundary. Its address and the GeoSearch address differ.
EPA facility registry
The registry point falls inside the lot. ECHO lists a calculated location accuracy of 372 meters for that point.
Water discharge permit
ECHO’s published permit location falls inside the lot. The permit ID also appears in the state ruling.
Waste program record
ECHO links this record to the facility. Its published point is about 9.5 meters outside the lot.
Waste program record
ECHO links this record to the facility. Its published point is about 10.8 meters outside the lot.

blocks.text: We tested all seven coordinate-bearing rows in the ECHO report’s registry and program listing against the MapPLUTO polygon. Five points were covered by the lot and two fell outside. We normalized the reported datums to WGS84 and measured the distance from each outside point to the polygon in UTM zone 18N. These distances describe the published points relative to that version of the boundary. Review the original program records before attributing equipment or an activity to the parcel.

blocks.label: Download the tax lot, source points, and permit cross-reference

sections.heading: Read the dates behind permit and enforcement status

blocks.text: The ECHO snapshot retrieved November 22, 2026 labels water permit NY0026204 effective and lists June 30, 2027 as its expiration date. It also links a second water permit, NY0276570, with a terminated status. Keep the two identifiers and their status fields separately. For a decision that depends on a permit’s conditions or continued coverage, obtain the final permit and any modifications from the state.

For NY0026204, ECHO reports its significant noncompliance flag as “No” as of June 30, 2026. The same snapshot lists a state notice of violation dated August 24, 2026. The two records answer different questions and have different dates. Open the underlying notice and any later case documents to verify what it concerns and how it was resolved.

On the air side, the publicly available document for 2-6101-00025/00100 is marked draft and has blank effective and expiration date fields on its first page. Save that document as a draft and locate the signed version before relying on its conditions. A separate EPA Superfund profile for Newtown Creek covers a waterway and its tributaries. Follow that record under its own site ID when researching nearby cleanup history.

sections.heading: Build a diligence file that another reviewer can check

blocks.text: Create one record per document or dated database observation. Include the parcel or candidate area, facility and program IDs, operator, record type, document date, source URL, retrieval date, and the reason you linked it to the site. Keep unresolved matches visible. An enforcement notice and the order that resolves it should retain their own dates and relationship.

Use this file for preliminary screening and to frame the questions for the environmental professional and the issuing agency. For a transaction that calls for a Phase I environmental site assessment or All Appropriate Inquiries, review EPA’s requirements for the applicable process. Site history, interviews, records review, and physical inspection serve purposes beyond a permit lookup.

title: Data center site selection tools for power capacity
description: Compare six power screening tools for a 200 MW data center. See how a South Carolina docket separates load plans, upgrades, and actual energization.
coverAlt: Diagram of the Aiken No. 3 to Mt. Zion transmission buildout. A 16.2-mile section leads to the Mt. Zion switching station. Two feeders totaling 1.5 miles lead to customer substations. The first energized on December 15, 2025.
coverCaption: Simplified transmission scope for the Aiken project. The South Carolina Public Service Commission granted certificates in July 2024. Santee Cooper later reported the first customer substation energized in December 2025.
intro: For a 200 MW data center, use a power screening tool to compare where you could connect, how much load each point can support under a stated study case, and what has to happen before each phase. Start with a site search or sourced grid report, then get a study that tests your actual load profile. Before committing to a site or promising a date, ask the serving utility for the documents behind the MW, the upgrades, and the schedule.
takeaways: Compare tools on the same site, load ramp and target dates. Ask which connection points, planning cases, prior requests and outages drive each answer.
Keep modeled load capacity, signed service terms, construction and energization as separate steps.

For a planned 200 MW project in South Carolina, the accepted connection required work across two transmission owners and customer substations. The utility later reported that one substation had energized while the other had a revised target window.

sections.heading: Which power screening tool fits the decision?

blocks.text: Use the comparison to choose a starting point for procurement. It describes what each provider publishes about its tools as of November 22, 2026. Invariant publishes this guide. The South Carolina example comes from the public docket. It is independent of the provider descriptions.

columns: What to ask for on the same 200 MW site
rows: Paces
Portfolio and parcel screening with regional withdrawal-capacity views, plus project reports and support for interconnection applications.
Ask how the regional capacity layer was calculated. Request a worked report with the selected connection, modeled phase MW, dependencies, and an explanation of how it arrived at its dates.
Geoforge

Site reports combine offtake capacity by year and scenario, modeled on ISO/RTO grid cases as described by the provider, with queue context and planned upgrades. Its example shows a connection shortlist and an estimated time-to-power range.
Ask which loads and upgrades were included in each scenario. Have the provider show how the timeline changes if a named upgrade slips or a competing request advances.
PVcase Prospect
Map-based screening using modeled withdrawal capacity. Its capacity documentation explains the use of planning scenarios and a focus on later-stage queue projects.
Confirm the exact substation bus, constraint scenario and year. Ask which projects were included and how the report handles a load larger than the displayed withdrawal capacity.
GridCARE
Grid simulation and utility collaboration to identify underused capacity. Its National Grid announcement describes an effort to identify capacity for large loads in New York.
Confirm the utility and service area for your site. Ask what flexibility or curtailment the case assumes, how many MW would be available in each phase, and who can approve the service terms.
Mireye
Cited location and infrastructure data, including substations, transmission voltage classes and site screening bundles.
Use it to identify nearby candidates and inspect sources. Ask separately for evidence behind any MW figure or service date you intend to carry into underwriting.
Invariant

Earth provides parcel and grid context. The published study workflow describes AC power flow and loss-of-one-element contingency tests by connection and study year, with indicative upgrade costs and timing.
Ask which cases are reconstructed or supplied by a utility, how the model was checked, and what evidence supports each phase and its cost range.

blocks.text: Treat the date from a screening report as an estimate with a source and assumptions. A queue entry records a request or study status, depending on the system. Ask whether the product shows large loads, generation, or both, and which requests were actually included in the planning case. Operators publish different amounts of load information. For example, ERCOT has a separate large-load integration process.

sections.heading: Aiken County shows what a 200 MW connection takes

blocks.text: Central Electric Power Cooperative’s application in South Carolina PSC docket 2024-61-E identified a planned data center with up to 200 MW of peak demand. It described a large-power service agreement entered in September 2023. Santee Cooper initially considered a 115 kV connection. According to testimony cited in the commission’s order, that option required significant upgrades, and 230 kV service was expected to be faster and more cost-effective for the customer.

columns: What to carry into a site comparison
rows: Approved transmission scope · July 23, 2024
The order describes two 230 kV lines on the 16.2-mile Aiken No. 3 to Mt. Zion route. Central’s two lines from Mt. Zion to customer substations total about 1.5 miles.
Track the upstream buildout, switching station, feeders and customer work separately. A map of the lead line alone would miss the upstream work.
Construction complete · reported December 9, 2025
Santee Cooper later cited its December filing reporting completion of the transmission lines, switching station and Central feeder lines.
File the utility’s report against the scope it names. Keep commissioning stages and site works as separate milestones.
First customer substation energized · December 15, 2025
Santee Cooper confirmed the date in an April 2, 2026 filing.
Mark the first substation’s energization. The selected filing gives the date and leaves the MW energized at that stage unspecified.
Second date revised · April 2, 2026 filing
Santee Cooper reported that the customer requested a May or June 2026 window for the second substation.
Save the revised window as a request. Use a subsequent utility record to establish actual energization.

blocks.text: There were 510 days between the certificate and the first reported energization. The project record explains the work between those dates. At Aiken, the presence of a 115 kV line would have identified a corridor. The chosen buildout added 230 kV facilities on that corridor, a switching station, and customer feeders. For a new site, ask what could change the ranking of connection options, including outage resilience and any shared routes or equipment.

blocks.label: Download the Aiken milestones and links to the source filings

sections.heading: How to test tools with the same load and site

blocks.text: Give each provider the same parcel and a load ramp stated in total utility MW. An illustrative request might be 50 MW in 2027, 120 MW in 2028, and 200 MW in 2029. If your requirement starts with IT load, explicitly include the facility loads and operating assumptions that determine what the utility must deliver. Supply the critical-load requirement, operating flexibility, and whether on-site generation can support any phase.

items: Ask for every plausible point of interconnection, including connection voltage, transmission owner, feasible route, and which utility should receive the request. Keep distance and load capacity in their own fields.

For each phase, ask for the base case, year, relevant seasonal cases, load scenarios, and contingency assumptions. Request the limiting equipment and modeled headroom in MW. Record the grid data vintage and any missing inputs.

Ask which existing and proposed loads, generators, and transmission upgrades are included. Track queue status and identify the upgrades required for each phase, who pays, and which schedule events can change the result.
Keep signed service terms, clearing and construction approvals, procurement steps, and energization evidence in a dated file. Assign follow-up to the party that can confirm the next milestone.

blocks.text: Compare the output at the decision you need to make. For an initial shortlist, a documented reason to investigate or rule out a site may be enough. For an option payment or a tenant delivery commitment, get the utility’s written assessment, the service terms, and a milestone schedule tied to your load. Keep any unresolved assumptions visible to the team making the commitment.

title: Manufacturing site selection for 100 buildable acres
description: Find industrial sites with rail, water, wastewater and power. Use a South Carolina case to check parcel size, utility service, and what’s ready to build.
coverAlt: Three Camp Hall Campus 9 records. A 2023 exhibit shows 90.94 acres overall, a 2025 brochure shows 124.3 total acres for parcels 6 and 7, and the listing viewed in November 2026 reports 120 acres available.
coverCaption: Camp Hall publishes three acreage figures with different descriptions. Use the current offering boundary and the project layout to measure how much contiguous land will work for the plant.
intro: To find an industrial site with at least 100 buildable acres, start with state and utility site inventories and get the boundary of each tract actually on offer. Screen contiguous land, the path to rail, water and wastewater service, and phased utility power. Ask for a dated document behind each pass. A site can have enough total acres and still fail to fit the plant, yard, and rail siding in one usable layout.
takeaways: Ask for 100 contiguous buildable acres with the footprint, yard, access and easements accounted for. Check availability on the same boundary you use for the layout.
Ask the railroad and utilities to confirm the connection point, the required improvements and the date service can start.

At Camp Hall Campus 9, a 2023 exhibit, a 2025 brochure and the listing reviewed in November 2026 show different acreage descriptions. The 120 listed available acres leave 20 acres above a 100-acre requirement before checking the layout.

sections.heading: What to use for a first manufacturing shortlist

blocks.text: Use state and local economic development inventories to find candidate properties and the people who maintain their data. South Carolina’s LocateSC is one example. Start with the geography and your must-have traits, then get the current offering boundary, seller or option holder, and date behind each listing. Read the certification materials for any site advertised as certified. They tell you which studies were available for the program and what you can request.

rows: 100 buildable acres
County parcel GIS, state site inventories, USGS terrain, mapped flood hazards and wetlands.
Current sale or lease boundary, survey, field delineation where needed, and a concept layout with required buffers and grading.
Freight rail
Bureau of Transportation Statistics rail network data, the carrier’s service map, and the industrial park’s track plan.
Serving carrier, usable siding or turnout, switching plan, railcar volume the carrier can handle, and a schedule for service or needed construction.
Process water
Utility service-area maps, site utility plans, and the water provider’s records.
Tie-in location, available average and peak flow, pressure and fire flow, water quality, cost, and service date.
Industrial wastewater
The receiving sewer utility and its industrial pretreatment program, or the applicable discharge permitting authority.
Accepted flow and characteristics of the proposed waste stream, pretreatment needs, pump or line upgrades, and the applicable approval.
Electric service
Serving utility and transmission owner, mapped facilities, and public project or study records.
MW by phase, point of service, supply and reliability terms, required upgrades, cost responsibility, and service dates.

sections.heading: How to test the 100-acre requirement

blocks.text: Start with the surveyed or proposed tract boundary. Map where the layout can’t go, including relevant wetlands and setbacks, recorded easements, terrain outside the grading plan, and road or utility corridors. Examine overlapping exclusions together so you subtract each area once. Then keep the geometry and area of each connected piece. The areas you can use for circulation, utilities, and drainage depend on the design and any applicable approval.

For example, a site could have 110 acres left after exclusions in two blocks of 65 and 45 acres. Its largest block is 65 acres. A project that needs 100 contiguous acres needs a different layout or a different tract. Put the proposed building, laydown and truck yards, loading tracks, and access routes on the plan before clearing the acreage requirement.

sections.heading: Camp Hall Campus 9 has three acreage descriptions

blocks.text: Camp Hall’s Campus 9 page links both an older site exhibit and a marketing brochure. We checked the listing and both files for the area each actually describes. The PDFs give overall acreage for the land they depict. The listing distinguishes the original developable acreage from the acres sold and those it still offers.

rows: Site exhibit · February 2023
90.94 acres
The overall total printed on the exhibit. It also shows a separately labeled parcel and a utility service territory boundary.
Campus 9 brochure · January 2025
124.3 acres
The overall acreage described for parcels 6 and 7. The brochure also describes water, sewer, and roads as work in progress for the site.
Site listing · checked November 22, 2026
120 acres
The acreage the owner lists as available. It reports 147 original developable acres and 27 sold.

blocks.text: The 120 available acres give a 20-acre margin over a 100-acre requirement on paper. Ask the owner for the current boundary of the 120 acres and the survey or acreage calculation behind it. Run the project layout on that boundary. The older exhibit and brochure help explain why a site name alone is an unreliable key for acreage.

The utility evidence has its own dates. The brochure describes a 12-inch water line design along Camp Hall Boulevard. The listing says water and sewer are in place and its site details describe adjacency to a future substation. The older exhibit shows two electric service territories. These records provide leads for provider calls. Confirm the connection applicable to the offered tract and ask for the capacity and service date in writing.

Palmetto Railways describes a 25-mile corridor connecting the commerce park to the CSX main line, with construction through fall 2026 on the page we reviewed. For a rail-served plant, ask if the corridor is in service and whether the railroad can accept and switch the proposed cars to the tract. Get the location and status of the siding or proposed turnout and the scope of any connection work.

sections.heading: What to verify before paying for an option

blocks.text: Send the same requirements to each site contact. Include the minimum contiguous area, what needs to fit, railcar types and volumes, water and wastewater needs, and the MW and dates for each phase. Put the evidence next to each site in the shortlist. Use a current drawing for the property, a carrier response for rail, and utility responses for service and timeline. Record who can answer each open question and when the buyer needs the answer.

title: Warehouse site selection for rail, trucks and trailer parking
description: Screen warehouse sites for a usable rail spur, legal truck routes and trailer parking. Use a Joliet case to verify property details and price tolls.
coverAlt: Aerial map of 3801 and 3750 CenterPoint Way in Joliet, Illinois. The owner’s map pins are about a quarter mile apart. The listings report 133 and 256 trailer spaces respectively, with rail access marked No at both properties.
coverCaption: Two CenterPoint Way listings in Joliet. The map shows the owner’s location pins. Aerial imagery from USDA and USGS The National Map.
intro: To screen a warehouse for rail and truck access, start with the specific loading doors, yard, and gate you would lease. Find the railroad and route that can serve those doors, check a truck route from the interstate to the actual gate, and count the trailer spaces your operation can use at its busiest hour. Nearby tracks and a large parking count are useful leads. Verify each requirement at the property before using it to select a site.
takeaways: If you need railcars at the building, get the turnout, siding, and carrier’s switching terms for that exact property. Intermodal terminal access supports a different operation.
Route the actual vehicle to the correct gate. Check clearance, posted limits, turns, and tolls along every segment.
Two Joliet properties about a quarter mile apart list 133 and 256 trailer spaces. The owner marks rail access as No at both, even though Union Pacific lists an intermodal terminal on the same road.

sections.heading: What data finds a warehouse with usable access?

rows: Direct rail siding
North American Rail Network lines and trackage rights, carrier service maps, and the site plan.
The carrier’s confirmation it can spot your railcars at the specific siding. Request track condition, usable length, car types, switching schedule, and who is responsible for repairs or construction.
Intermodal or transload access
Rail terminal directory and operating information from the carrier or transload operator.
The terminal or facility that accepts your freight, who handles the transfer or truck leg, what equipment they can accept, and the route between the facility and your gate.
Interstate truck access
State designated truck routes, local road and clearance records, and a routing API such as HERE configured for your truck dimensions and weights.
The route for the intended vehicle, including each jurisdiction, posted weight and clearance, allowed turns, toll, and any temporary restrictions. Confirm the route to the gate in use.
Trailer parking and gate access
Property listing, current site plan, lease plan, and the operator’s yard records.
Dedicated positions by type and size, peak parked trailers, docks and staging reserved for other uses, turning envelope, and gate throughput.

blocks.text: A rail spur is a track connection that can let the carrier deliver cars to a particular site. At an intermodal terminal, a container can move between rail and truck. At a transload facility, freight can be transferred between the railcar and the truck. Decide which operation your business needs, then verify the facility and route that can actually provide it.

sections.heading: Two properties on the same road in Joliet

blocks.text: Union Pacific lists its Global 4 Intermodal Terminal at 3000 CenterPoint Way in Joliet, Illinois. We checked two CenterPoint property listings on the same road. Their published map pins are about 399 meters apart in a straight line, about one quarter mile. We measured between the owner’s pins using the WGS84 ellipsoid. The result describes proximity, and the site gates and road route are separate checks.

rows: 3801 CenterPoint Way
No
3750 CenterPoint Way
No

blocks.text: For a tenant that needs railcars at the building, the terminal address offers evidence of intermodal infrastructure in the area. Ask the owner and carrier about direct service to the exact tract. For a tenant using containers by truck, check the route to the terminal and confirm operating and access terms. The parking count belongs to each listed property. Confirm which spaces the proposed lease actually includes.

sections.heading: Check the truck route to the gate and price each crossing

blocks.text: Use the proposed gate as the endpoint. Start with a truck routing service that accepts the complete vehicle profile. Compare its result with state and local designations and the route conditions the carrier can confirm. Check ramps and turns, underpasses, posted limits, and the road between the interchange and yard. Record the equipment type, the date and the authority behind each restriction.

The Houbolt Road Extension provides a tolled connection between I-80 and CenterPoint Intermodal Center. Its schedule effective April 1, 2026 lists a Class 3 toll of $9.15 with a qualifying transponder and $14.65 without one. At 200 tollable Class 3 crossings, the illustrative totals are $1,830 and $2,930. Price the route using the operator’s vehicle class and payment method, and recheck the schedule before contracting for the truck moves.

sections.heading: Measure trailer parking at the busiest point in the shift

blocks.text: Start with the spaces reserved for your operation on the current lease plan. Check whether the longest trailers fit, whether access lanes stay clear, and how many spots are taken by staging, maintenance, or shared operations. Then track arrivals, departures, and trailer dwell by time of day. Use your highest simultaneous count of parked trailers to size the yard.

In an illustrative layout with 133 marked positions, reserving 12 for staging and taking six out of service leaves 115 for parked trailers. If 118 need to park at the same time, the layout is three short. The reservations and peak count are example assumptions. Bring a current yard plan and a peak operating schedule to the site visit so you can test your own numbers.

faqs.answer: Use property and rail maps to shortlist sites with a plausible track connection. Ask the serving railroad for confirmation that your cars can be spotted at that siding, along with track condition, usable length, switching frequency, and any work needed.

faqs.question: Does being near an intermodal terminal mean a warehouse is rail-served?

faqs.question: How many trailer spaces does a warehouse need?

coverCaption: Equinix lists NY4 and NY5 at different addresses. AWS lists NY4 as an access option for the NY5 Direct Connect location. The diagram shows the directory relationship.
intro: To verify fiber route diversity at a data center, identify the exact endpoints of both circuits and ask the providers for evidence of their physical paths. Check the building entrances, internal paths, outside conduits and crossings, and where each circuit hands off to the next network. A directory can tell you which carriers or cloud services to investigate. For a lease or service commitment, document what the surviving circuit can carry when one route or facility fails.
takeaways: Look up the exact building and service address. Record the carrier, underlying operator, connection endpoint, and whether the proposed service has been ordered or built.
At Secaucus, Equinix lists two different building addresses, while AWS lists one Direct Connect location for the access relationship shown in this example.
Check both route separation and surviving throughput. Two 10 Gbps circuits leave 10 Gbps of nominal capacity after a single circuit loss.

sections.heading: What can you verify from a data center address?

rows: Who reports service nearby?
FCC National Broadband Map for reported fixed availability and operator service maps or quotes.
Exact building, provider, technology, and date. Ask the carrier to qualify the specific service and endpoint.
Which network or cloud handoffs are offered?
Facility operator pages, its connectivity contacts, and the cloud provider’s location directory.
Building ID, named handoff location, connection product, underlying carrier where known, and the organization providing the interconnect.
What is the physical route for each circuit?
A carrier route exhibit or a written route comparison for the proposed or installed circuits, including both endpoints.
Path and entrance identifiers, common segments, route version, associated circuit order, and the comparison scope.
What survives a loss or scheduled maintenance?
Service terms, circuit design, equipment and port assignments, and a coordinated acceptance test.
Agreed failures to test, surviving throughput and failover behavior, observation date, exceptions, and the owner of any remediation.

blocks.text: A carrier name by itself leaves several questions open. Ask who owns and operates the access segment and whether either provider leases facilities from the same third party. In a multi-building campus, confirm the service address, point of entry, handoff room and equipment for the specific circuit you intend to buy.

blocks.text: The count depends on what you’re counting. For NY4 and NY5, the public records establish two buildings and one named AWS location in this comparison. If your design requires two AWS locations, use the cloud provider’s location records to choose candidates, then verify the transport from your site to each handoff. The next evidence you need is the route comparison for the two circuits you plan to order.

sections.heading: How to verify two independent fiber paths

blocks.text: Draw the comparison from your equipment to the two remote handoffs. Check the building entrances, risers, cross-connect rooms, conduit, and any crossings where the routes could come back together. Include shared access equipment and maintenance domains where those risks matter to your design. Network engineers sometimes call links that share a physical failure risk a shared-risk link group.

items: Ask both providers for current route exhibits or a written comparison that names the circuit orders, endpoints, and parts of the path covered. Use the providers’ agreed process for reviewing sensitive drawings.
Ask for exceptions in writing. A shared conduit, building entrance, or wholesale local loop may affect both circuits. Identify what fails together and whether the design accepts that risk.
Compare the installed route and endpoint records at acceptance, then track changes to the route or the facility. Confirm the contracted installation scope and any notification terms for rerouting.

blocks.text: The AWS Direct Connect resiliency models also distinguish device failures from complete location failures. Pick the level of resilience your workload requires, including any separate facility or device requirements, and verify the last-mile design that connects your equipment to those AWS locations.

sections.heading: Can the surviving circuit carry the workload?

blocks.text: Suppose two nominal 10 Gbps circuits must carry a 15 Gbps peak workload after either one fails. With one down, 10 Gbps of nominal capacity remains and the shortfall is 5 Gbps. This example uses link rates before protocol overhead. Use measured usable capacity and your own traffic profile for procurement.

Agree on an acceptance test with the providers. Exercise each failure the contract and design are meant to cover in a coordinated window, then record which path carried traffic, the transition time, and delivered throughput at the expected load. Keep the test evidence and the route evidence together so a reviewer can see both the physical design and what happened during failover.

faqs.question: Can I look up exact fiber routes by address?
faqs.answer: An address lookup can identify reported providers, facilities, and cloud access locations. Ask the proposed providers for a route comparison tied to your circuit orders and endpoints. Verify building entry and shared physical segments as part of that review.

faqs.question: Do two carriers guarantee two physical fiber paths?
faqs.answer: Check the actual routes and facility handoffs for both carriers. Different service providers can share the same underlying conduit, local access facilities, or building entrances. Ask each provider which parts of the path its diversity commitment covers.

faqs.question: Do two 10 Gbps circuits support 15 Gbps after one fails?
faqs.answer: On nominal rates, one surviving 10 Gbps circuit leaves a 5 Gbps shortfall against a 15 Gbps requirement. Check measured throughput and failover behavior under the workload you plan to carry.
